But if not, etc. To explain what was already explained in seif 8 that if she did not comb her immersion did not count even if nothing interposing was found on her — only because the opening [of the section] holds it. Derishah. And Bach wrote that we deal where she combed her head but not her entire body, for the body there is only ordinary custom as above s.k. 2; and if she immersed b'dieved her immersion counted; but if something interposing was found on her, even b'dieved her immersion did not count even though she dealt with that kind. And likewise Tosafot and Agudah there in the name of Rabbenu Tam — that this Chullin deals in other places on the body that she did not comb them; and the text teaches "something interposing was found on her" — apparently specifically when something interposing was found on her, for if not so her immersion counted. And what Ran z"l wrote implies their way was to rinse with hot water; and so it appears to me — we say if she immersed close to chafifah she need not comb and immerse; and if it were so that they do chafifah only in place of hair, why would we be concerned perhaps she did not examine well other places on the body as we are concerned when it was not close to immersion (for regarding examination)? All other places on the body are certainly one matter — except their way was to rinse their entire body with hot water — end quote; and Beit Yosef brings it. This refers to "something interposing was found on her" — but when nothing interposing was found on her there is to distinguish between the head and other places on the body — for although she did not comb them, since she examined them her immersion counted b'dieved.

turei_zahav.he: אבל אם לא חפפה קודם טבילה כו'. כן כתב הטור רבים מקשים דהא אפילו לא נמצא כלל דבר חוצץ לא עלתה לה טבילה כשלא חפפה תחילה כמ"ש סעיף ח' ונ"ל לתרץ דג' חלוקות יש בזה דאם תוך העונה שחפפה טבלה אין צריך טבילה אחרת ואם יש עונה צריכה טבילה אחרת אא"כ נתעסקה אח"כ והיינו שעל כל פנים אין בין חפיפה לטבילה אלא עונה אחת אבל אם יש ביניהם הרבה כגון שחפפה בע"ש וטבלה מוצ"ש דחפיפה זו לא מיקרי קודם טבילה כלל אלא רחוק ממנה אז לא מהני נתעסקה אח"כ וע"כ כתב בזה לא חפפה קודם טבילה ר"ל אלא רחוק ממנה הרבה כנ"ל:
turei_zahav.en: However, if she did not wash and comb before immersion, etc. So wrote the Tur. Many ask that even if no intervening substance at all was found, her immersion is invalid when she did not first wash and comb, as stated in seif 8. It appears to me that there are three distinctions. If she immersed within the same onah in which she washed and combed, she does not require another immersion. If one onah intervened, she requires another immersion unless she engaged afterward in something that could have produced the substance. This means that in any event no more than one onah intervened between the washing and combing and immersion. If, however, a much longer interval intervened, such as where she washed and combed on erev Shabbos and immersed on Motzei Shabbos, that washing and combing is not considered to have been performed before immersion at all, for it was very distant from it. In such a case, even if she later engaged in something that could have produced the substance, the earlier washing and combing does not help. Therefore, the Tur writes here, “she did not wash and comb before immersion,” meaning that she did so only a long time beforehand, as explained.

baer_heitev.he:
תולה. והש"ך פסק דאין תולין להקל עד שאמרה ברי לי שלא היה עלי בשעת טבילה וכן הוא ממש דעת כל הפוסקים וכן העיקר לדינא וכ"פ הב"ח:
אבל. והא דכתב בס"ח דאם לא חפפה לא עלתה לה טבילה אפילו לא נמצא עליה דבר החוצץ תירץ הב"ח דמיירי כאן שחפפה ראשה אבל לא כל גופה דבגופה ליכא אלא מנהגא בעלמא ואם טבלה בדיעבד עלתה לה טבילה אבל נמצא עליה דבר חוצץ אפילו דיעבד לא עלתה לה טבילה אע"פ שנתעסקה באותו המין והט"ז מתרץ דג' חלוקות יש בדבר דאם תוך העונה שחפפה טבלה א"צ טבילה אחרת ואם יש עונה צריכה טבילה אחרת אא"כ נתעסקה אח"כ והיינו שעכ"פ אין בין חפיפה לטבילה רק עונה א' אבל אם יש ביניהם הרבה כגון שחפפה בערב שבת וטבלה במ"ש דחפיפה זו לא מקרי קודם טבילה כלל אלא רחוק ממנה אז לא מהני נתעסקה אח"כ וע"כ כתב בזה לא חפפה קודם טבילה ר"ל אלא רחוק ממנה הרבה עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en:
Attributes. Shach rules that she may not attribute the substance leniently unless she can state with certainty that it was not present during immersion. This is the view of the authorities and Bach.
But. And that which is written in Shach — if she did not comb, her immersion did not count even if nothing interposing was found on her — Bach answers that here we deal where she combed her head but not her entire body; for the body there is only an ordinary custom, and if she immersed b'dieved her immersion counted. But if something interposing was found on her, even b'dieved her immersion did not count, even though she dealt with that kind. And Taz answers that there are three distinctions: if within the onah that she combed she immersed, she does not need another immersion; if there is [another] onah she needs another immersion unless she dealt with it afterward — meaning at least there is only one onah between combing and immersion. But if there are many between them, such as she combed on erev Shabbat and immersed on motza'ei Shabbat, this combing is not called before immersion at all but rather far from it — then dealing with it afterward does not help. And therefore he wrote in this "did not comb before immersion" — meaning only far from it a lot — end quote.

beer_hagolah.he:
טור מדברי הרשב"א בת"ה וכתב הב"י וטעמו מדתניא פ"ק דחולין דף י' ע"א טבל ועלה וכו' והוא תמוה לענ"ד דמהדר אהיתרא והביא ראיה לאיסורא ואדרבה צ"ל לדעת הרשב"א דההיא ברייתא לטהרות מיירי וכמ"ש התוס' שם בשם ר"ח דלטהרות החמירו יותר מלבעלה וכו' אבל הרמב"ם בספ"ב מהלכות מקואות מפרשה שה"ה לבעלה ופסק כוותיה דלא עלתה לה טבילה אא"כ אומרת ברי לי שלא היתה עלי קודם לכן וכ"כ הרשב"א שם בשם הראב"ד:
טור ופי' הרב ט"ז שחפפה ביום שלפני פניו כגון שחפפה בע"ש וטבלה במ"ש דאי לא חפפה כלל הא כתב לעיל בסעיף ח' אפילו עינה ובדקה עצמה מיד אחר הטבילה לא עלתה לה טבילה והרב ב"ח פי' בע"א עי"ש:
beer_hagolah.en:
The Tur from the words of the Rashba in Torat HaBayit. Beit Yosef writes that his reason is the baraita in Chullin 10a concerning one who immersed and ascended. In my humble opinion, this is astonishing, because he returns to the lenient ruling while bringing proof for stringency. Rather, according to the Rashba, that baraita must concern matters of ritual purity, as Tosafot writes there in the name of Rabbeinu Chananel, that greater stringency was applied to ritual purity than to a woman's permissibility to her husband. Rambam, however, at the end of chapter 2 of Hilchot Mikvaot, interprets it as applying equally to her husband and rules that her immersion is invalid unless she says with certainty that the interposition was not upon her beforehand. The Rashba likewise cites this in the name of the Raavad.
The Tur. The Taz explains that she washed on the preceding day, such as on Friday and immersed after Shabbat. If she did not wash at all, the Tur already wrote above in seif 8 that even if she inspected herself immediately after immersion, the immersion is invalid. Bach explains it differently. See there.

beur_hagra.he: בד"א כו'. עתוס' שם ד"ה אם סמוך כו' והא דאמר כו' התם בשלא כו' ועוד אור"י כו' ונ"מ בין תירוץ זה לתי' קמא דבתי' זה נתעסקה תלינן טפי אפי' לא טבלה סמוך לחפיפה דדוקא לא חפפה כלל אלא בעיוני בעלמא שהוא ד"ת ונקט הרשב"א והטור כהאי תי' ומ"מ דבריהם צ"ע דבלא חפפה כלל בלא"ה צריכה טבילה אחרת כנ"ל ס"ח ולכן כתבו תוס' לטהרות ועש"ך. ורמב"ם כתב הברייתא כפשטה וכשיטתו דאין חילוק אלא בחפיפה וא"צ לתי' של תוס' וש"ע בסעיף י' כתב דברי הרמב"ם וכאן כתב שיטת הפוסקים:
beur_hagra.en: When does this apply, etc. See Tosafot there, s.v. im samuch, etc.: that which the Gemara says, etc., refers to a case where she did not, etc. Rabbeinu Yitzchak further explains, etc. The practical difference between this answer and the first answer is that according to this answer, if she subsequently handled a substance that might adhere, we are more inclined to attribute the intervening matter to that activity, even where she did not immerse immediately after chafifah. The case is specifically one where she performed no chafifah at all, but merely inspected herself, which is a Torah requirement. The Rashba and Tur adopt this answer. Nevertheless, their words require study, for if she performed no chafifah at all, she must in any event immerse again, as explained above in seif 8. Tosafot therefore explain the passage as referring to matters of ritual purity. See Shach. The Rambam cites the baraita in its plain sense, in accordance with his approach that the distinction concerns only chafifah, and he therefore does not require Tosafot’s answer. In seif 10 the Shulchan Aruch records the Rambam’s ruling, whereas here it records the view of the other poskim.

siftei_kohen.he:
אם לא עיינה. וכ"ש אם לא חפפה:
תולין להקל. ע"ל סימן קצ"ח ס"ק ל"ג כתבתי דהרוקח חולק:
siftei_kohen.en:
If she did not examine. And all the more if she did not perform chafifah.
We attribute to be lenient. See above siman 198 s.k. 33 where I wrote that Rokeach disagrees.

baer_heitev.he: עיינה. וכ"ש אם לא חפפה תולין להקל וע"ל סימן קצ"ח דהרוקח חולק ע"ז ופסק שאין תולין להקל. ש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: Examined. All the more so if she did not wash, one may attribute leniently. Shach notes that Rokeach disagrees and requires stringency.

beer_hagolah.en: There in the name of the Raavad.

beur_hagra.he: בד"א כו'. כיון שא"צ עיון בדיעבד כנ"ל ס"ט וצ"ע:
beur_hagra.en: When does this apply, etc. Since after the fact she does not require inspection, as explained above in seif 9. This requires study.

siftei_kohen.he:
או שנתנה לבנה תבשיל כו'. והיכא דהיה ביד בנה תבשיל א"נ היה מלוכלך בטיט ולקחה בנה על ידיה ערומה ואחר כך טבלה ולא עיינה נפשה לא עלתה לה טבילה דדמי לנתנה תבשיל לבנה. ב"ח:
אבל מותרת ללבוש כו'. דלא דמי לנתנה תבשיל שאין רגילות להיות על הבגדים דבר לח לידבק בגוף האשה. שם:
siftei_kohen.en:
Or she gave her son a cooked dish, etc. And where her son had a cooked dish in hand, or he was dirty with mud, and he took her son by her bare hands, and afterward she immersed and did not examine herself — her immersion did not count, for it is similar to giving a cooked dish to her son — Bach.
But she is permitted to put on, etc. For it is not comparable to giving a cooked dish — for it is not common for clothing to have something moist that would adhere to the woman's body — ibid.

baer_heitev.he:
תבשיל. והיכא שהיה ביד בנה תבשיל א"נ היה מלוכלך בטיט ולקחה בנה על ידה ערומה ואח"כ טבלה ולא עיינה נפשה לא עלתה לה טבילה דדמי לנתנה תבשיל לבנה. ב"ח:
בגדיה. דל"ד לנתנה תבשיל לבנה שאין רגילות להיות על הבגדים דבר לח לידבק בגוף האשה. שם:
baer_heitev.en:
A cooked dish. If her child held food or was covered with mud and she lifted the child against her bare body, then immersed without examining herself, the immersion is invalid, like one who gave food to her child. Bach.
Her clothing. This differs from giving food to a child because wet substances do not ordinarily remain on clothing and transfer to the woman's body. Bach.

beer_hagolah.he:
מימרא דרב גידל אמר רב נדה דף ס"ז ע"א:
טור וכ"כ הרשב"א:
שם בגמרא:
beer_hagolah.en:
The statement of Rav Gidal in the name of Rav, Niddah 67a.
The Tur. The Rashba likewise writes this.
There in the Gemara.

beur_hagra.he:
חפפה כו'. ראב"ד ורשב"א דאל"כ בלא"ה לא עלתה כנ"ל ס"ח:
נתעסקה כו'. נלמד מהא דנתנה תבשיל כו' כמש"ו:
הראוי לידבק. רשב"א וטור ופשוט הוא:
לא עלתה כו'. כבר כתבתי בסי' הקודם (בליקוט שבס"ק מ"ד) שלדעת רמב"ם ותוס' עלתה טבילה ומה שרצה לידחק בב"י לדעת הרמב"ם דבדבר הנדבק מודה הרמב"ם דמ"ש ממפשלת כו' דבריו דחוקים דלא דמי זה לזה:
beur_hagra.en:
If she performed chafifah, etc. Raavad and Rashba. Otherwise, even apart from this concern, the immersion would not be valid, as explained above in seif 8.
If she handled, etc. This is derived from the case in which she gave a cooked dish, etc., as the Shulchan Aruch continues.
Something capable of adhering. Rashba and Tur. This is obvious.
The immersion was not valid, etc. I already wrote in the preceding siman, in the supplement to seif katan 44, that according to the Rambam and Tosafot the immersion is valid. The Beit Yosef attempts to explain the Rambam by distinguishing a substance that adheres, regarding which the Rambam would concede, from the case of a woman who carries her son, etc. His words are strained, because the two cases are not comparable.
